item.title: WordPress wp2shell RCE, HollowGraph Microsoft 365 C2, and Middle East Government Espionage
item.content:encoded:
CVE-2026-63030 & CVE-2026-60137: WordPress Core Pre-Authentication RCE Overview & Takeaways — Must Read

WordPress disclosed an actively exploited critical vulnerability chain affecting Core 6.9.0–6.9.4 and 7.0.0–7.0.1 that can allow unauthenticated full site takeover, with 6.8.0–6.8.5 also exposed to the SQL injection component. Site owners should immediately verify and apply the patched versions, block vulnerable REST API batch routes if needed, and check for compromise.

  • WordPress disclosed a critical vulnerability chain nicknamed “wp2shell” that combines CVE-2026-63030, a REST API Route Confusion issue, with CVE-2026-60137, a SQL Injection issue.
  • CVE-2026-63030 affects WordPress Core versions 6.9.0 through 6.9.4 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.1, while CVE-2026-60137 affects those versions plus WordPress Core versions 6.8.0 through 6.8.5.
  • When chained, the two vulnerabilities can result in unauthenticated SQL injection that grants complete control of an affected WordPress site, including access to all data, the ability to install malicious code, and full administrative access.
  • The article states that attackers are actively exploiting these vulnerabilities in the wild and that public proof-of-concept code became available on July 17, 2026.
  • The article recommends immediately updating to WordPress 7.0.2, 6.9.5, or 6.8.6 depending on the branch, and blocking both batch API paths if patching is delayed.

Targeted Attack on Government Entities in the Middle East | Part 1 — Should Read

Zscaler ThreatLabz detailed a July 2026 campaign by an East Asia-linked threat actor targeting Middle East government entities with a multi-stage malware chain using TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK. The attack abused Telegram for command and control, DLL sideloading, scheduled tasks, heavy obfuscation, anti-analysis checks, and environment-keyed payload encryption to maintain stealthy access.

  • In July 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz observed a threat actor with links to East Asia targeting government entities in the Middle East.
  • The campaign used a multi-stage attack chain beginning with an ISO file containing a legitimate ASUSTek RegSchdTask.exe file that sideloaded a malicious AsTaskSched.dll to deploy TELESHIM.
  • TELESHIM abused the Telegram API for command-and-control communication, validated a hardcoded chat ID, and supported command execution as well as download-and-execute messages.
  • TELESHIM and MIXEDKEY used heavy code obfuscation techniques including control flow flattening, mixed boolean arithmetic, and opaque predicates to hinder reverse engineering.
  • MIXEDKEY decrypted and reflectively loaded the final BINDCLOAK payload using two layers of XOR encryption, including a key derived from the infected machine’s volume serial number.

Hackers were inside South Korea's diplomat training system for 9 months — Should Read

Hackers breached South Korea’s Korea National Diplomatic Academy e-learning platform and remained inside for about nine months, stealing IDs, names, emails, and encrypted passwords of current and former foreign ministry personnel. Officials say the intrusion involved a zero-day flaw and misconfigured security settings, but the attacker and full scope of data exposure remain unknown.

  • Unidentified hackers compromised the Korea National Diplomatic Academy’s e-learning platform from April 2025 to February 2026.
  • South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the exposed data is believed to include trainee IDs, names, emails, and encrypted passwords, while contact details and personal photos were not affected.
  • The ministry shut down the e-learning system after being notified of abnormal access and said it has not restored the system since.
  • JoongAng Daily reported that the attacker exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in server software, compounded by misconfigured security settings.
  • The ministry said it has not attributed the attack to any specific threat actor and cannot yet determine precisely what information was accessed or exfiltrated.

HollowGraph Malware Hides C2 and Stolen Files in Microsoft 365 Events Dated 2050 — Should Read

HollowGraph is a newly discovered espionage implant that abuses a compromised Microsoft 365 calendar and Graph API traffic to hide commands and exfiltrated files in far-future calendar events dated 2050. Defenders should hunt for suspicious 2050 calendar entries, app-driven Graph activity, unusual AAAA DNS queries, and indicators like cloudlanecdn[.]com and logAzure.txt.

  • Group-IB discovered a .NET DLL espionage implant named HollowGraph that uses a hijacked Microsoft 365 calendar and Microsoft Graph API traffic as its command channel.
  • HollowGraph retrieves operator instructions from an attached file on a calendar event dated 2050-05-13 and exfiltrates stolen files by creating far-future calendar events with encrypted attachments.
  • The malware uses hybrid RSA and AES-256 encryption for calendar-based tasking and exfiltration, while a separate cleartext DNS channel refreshes Entra ID login details through IPv6 AAAA records from cloudlanecdn[.]com.
  • Group-IB ties HollowGraph to Cavern with high confidence based on shared command syntax and matching internal tasking, but it does not confidently attribute the campaign to any previously identified threat actor.
  • Group-IB found HollowGraph on at least 12 machines, with victim traffic observed from June 3 to July 9, 2026, and recommends hunting for far-future calendar events, suspicious calendar attachments, app-driven Microsoft Graph activity, cloudlanecdn[.]com, and logAzure.txt.

Romania races to restore land registry after cyberattack disrupts property market — Should Read

Romania is working to restore its fully digital land registry after a cyberattack knocked systems offline and froze property transactions nationwide, though officials say core cadastral and legal databases were not compromised. Authorities believe a financially motivated actor exploited known vulnerabilities and leaked credentials, with no evidence so far of stolen personal data.

  • Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration said a cyberattack disabled its central IT infrastructure, including the nationwide e-Terra cadastral and land registry platform.
  • The outage disrupted online land registry services, official email systems, and applications used by notaries, lawyers, cadastral specialists, and ANCPI employees, preventing new property transactions and existing requests from being processed.
  • ANCPI said its technical and legal databases containing cadastral information, ownership records, and mortgages had not been compromised.
  • The agency has begun migrating its applications to the Romanian government cloud and said services will be restored gradually after system integrity is verified.
  • Romania's National Directorate for Cyber Security said the attack appeared financially motivated and involved known software vulnerabilities and previously leaked credentials.

How a Fortune 500 media company blocked a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters attack using infrastructure flagged 24 hours before it launched — Should Read

Silent Push says a Fortune 500 media company blocked a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters social-engineering campaign because the attacker’s lookalike domain and related infrastructure had been flagged 24 hours before use. The company quickly pushed the mapped domains into CrowdStrike firewall controls, stopping a second attempt against another employee minutes later.

  • A Fortune 500 media and entertainment company stopped a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters attack because Silent Push had flagged the adversary infrastructure one day before the attack launched.
  • The threat actor called an employee and directed them to a lookalike domain impersonating a passkey authentication flow.
  • CrowdStrike detected the outbound connection attempt in firewall logs, and the organization used Silent Push to confirm the domain was an Indicator of Future Attack.
  • The organization used Silent Push to enumerate related campaign domains and pushed them into its CrowdStrike firewall within minutes.
  • Fifteen minutes after the initial domain was blocked, a second social engineering attempt against a different employee using a different domain was already blocked.

More than 1,000 domains illegally streaming World Cup games seized, DOJ says — May Read

The DOJ said U.S. and international law enforcement seized more than 1,000 domains that illegally streamed World Cup matches, warning that such sites can also expose users to malware and payment theft. The crackdown included operations tied to servers in Bulgaria and Peru and arrests in Colombia linked to the alleged cyber gang Los Ciberinfiltrados.

  • The Department of Justice announced that more than 1,000 domains illegally streaming World Cup games were seized over the course of the tournament.
  • The domains were disabled in three successive operations led by Homeland Security Investigations and the National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Center.
  • Federal officials said the effort was also aimed at reducing risks to consumers from malicious software embedded in many illicit streaming services.
  • The international investigation led to additional site takedowns across Argentina, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, the Dominican Republic and Colombia.
  • Colombian authorities arrested four suspected members of Los Ciberinfiltrados, a group accused of illegally accessing telecommunication systems and selling pirated streaming content including World Cup matches.

Email Security Needs Proof, Not Static Detection: Takeaways from SACR's Email Security Report — Optional

SACR’s report argues that email security must move beyond static link and attachment detection toward proof-driven analysis that follows phishing attacks through the full user journey. It highlights Varonis Interceptor as an example of this approach, using AI-driven sandboxing and contextual investigation to expose multi-step credential-harvesting attacks.

  • Software Analyst Cyber Research says email security must shift from detecting bad messages at the perimeter to investigating how an attack unfolds across identity, context, workflow, intent, and behavior.
  • The report says traditional perimeter-based email defenses are increasingly ineffective against modern attacks that lack obvious malicious links or attachments and can use AI-generated messages to abuse trusted relationships.
  • SACR highlights Varonis Interceptor as an example of this shift because it analyzes inbound communications with multiple detection layers, including language models, visual analysis, infrastructure inspection, URL detonation, and behavioral indicators.
  • The report says Varonis Interceptor’s AI Phishing Sandbox follows redirects, works through credential-capture forms, and surfaces multi-step attack paths to show what a user would actually encounter.
  • SACR argues that explainability is becoming a procurement requirement because organizations need evidence for why a platform reached a conclusion and how response decisions can be defended to executives, auditors, regulators, and cyber insurers.

What the Black Hat NOC Taught Me About MCP & Agentic SOCs (Chapter 3 of 4) | Corelight — Optional

The key takeaway is that MCP and agentic SOC workflows can help analysts move faster, but only if they are grounded in trusted telemetry, tight permissions, and human oversight. The Black Hat NOC experience highlights that agentic security tools should augment SOC teams rather than operate unchecked.

  • The article is titled “What the Black Hat NOC Taught Me About MCP & Agentic SOCs.”
  • The article is presented as Chapter 3 of a four-part series.
  • The article is associated with Corelight and refers to the Black Hat NOC.
  • The article’s title indicates that it discusses MCP and agentic SOCs in relation to lessons from the Black Hat NOC.

Health-ISAC Health Sector Heartbeat – Q2 2026 — Optional

Health-ISAC’s Q2 2026 Health Sector Heartbeat summarizes ransomware, cybercrime, targeted alert trends, underground forum activity, and the World Leaks threat actor as situational awareness for healthcare organizations. The key takeaway is that health sector organizations should review the report’s threat intelligence and mitigation guidance to better secure critical infrastructure.

  • Health-ISAC published its 2026 Second Quarter Health Sector Heartbeat on July 20, 2026.
  • The quarterly report provides observations on ransomware, cybercrime trends, and malicious actor forum postings that could potentially impact health sector organizations.
  • Health-ISAC states that the report is intended for situational awareness.
  • Health-ISAC recommends that members affiliated with victim companies or those potentially affected take appropriate measures to secure critical infrastructure.
  • The report includes sections on ransomware attacks in the health sector, targeted alert trends, underground forums activity, a threat actor profile of World Leaks, and mitigation strategies.

An AI SOC Evaluation Guide for Security Leaders — Optional

Security leaders evaluating AI SOC tools should look beyond polished demos and test whether the system produces reliable, explainable verdicts in their own environment with the identity, asset, and workflow context their analysts actually use. The article argues for human-AI hybrid evaluations that measure accuracy, analyst fit, durability, and safe escalation before production deployment.

  • The article says Gartner’s 2026 Hype Cycle for Security Operations placed AI SOC Agents at the Peak of Inflated Expectations after being at the Innovation Trigger stage with single-digit adoption the previous year.
  • Prophet Security worked with former Gartner analysts Oliver Rochford and Prateek Bhajanka on a vendor-agnostic guide for evaluating AI in the SOC.
  • The guide says AI SOC evaluations should test whether the AI can produce accurate verdicts in the organization’s own environment, especially using identity, asset, and organizational context for harder investigations such as privilege escalation or lateral movement.
  • The article recommends running AI SOC systems in parallel with human analysts, collecting baselines before deployment, and treating analyst overrides as important evaluation data.
  • The guide’s recommended model keeps humans and deterministic safeguards in control of containment, escalation, and irreversible actions while probabilistic AI handles triage and investigation.
